_meta.purpose: Illustrative STARTER seed for the Workforce Intelligence module. It shows the exact shape the loader expects and reminds you of the role/task/overlay/crosswalk relationships, so Phase 1 does not begin on a blank schema.
_meta.status: ILLUSTRATIVE — NOT production data. SFw role/task wording is representative, O*NET codes are plausible but MUST be verified, and ALL WORKBank desire/capability/HAS values are placeholders that MUST be replaced with real pulls before any client-facing use.

sources_of_truth.sfw_air_transport: https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/skills-framework/air-transport (export the Skills Map workbook; verify reuse terms)
sources_of_truth.onet: https://www.onetcenter.org/database.html (Task Statements, Tasks to DWAs; CC BY 4.0 with attribution)
sources_of_truth.workbank: https://github.com/SALT-NLP/workbank and the dataset on Hugging Face (read the Code Book for exact field semantics)

modelling_notes: WORKBank scores AI *agent* (software) automation/augmentation. It therefore maps cleanly to INFORMATION/COORDINATION tasks (documentation, reconciliation, load planning, rostering) and NOT to physical handling. Physical ramp tasks (loading, GSE operation) are a robotics / ground-support-equipment lever and are intentionally left WITHOUT an overlay row here — the pipeline must tag those 'model-inferred' and flag them as a different (non-agent) automation lever.
Keep has_level and capability_score INDEPENDENT. A task can be highly capable-to-automate yet sit at H4 because humans should stay in the loop (e.g. safety sign-off).
Every emitted score must carry a 'source' tag so the UI can show regulator-backed (SFw) and research-backed (WORKBank) versus model-inferred.
_meta.loader_note: This single combined file mirrors the four split files named in the spec (sfw_*, onet_subset, workbank_overlay, crosswalk). load_taxonomies.py may read either this combined file or the split files; upsert by the natural keys shown ('code' for sources, 'task_ref' for tasks, 'onet_task_code' for overlay).

Trace, document and process mishandled or delayed baggage and resolve passenger claims

Accept, document and process import and export cargo shipments against air waybills and customs documentation

Handle, classify and document dangerous goods in accordance with IATA regulations
Prepare the aircraft load instruction and loadsheet (weight and balance) and verify final load distribution for captain sign-off
Determine the quantity and orientation of cargo and oversee weight distribution for safe aircraft loading
Prepare and process documents for shipments, including waybills and customs and hazardous-materials paperwork

taxonomy_crosswalk.note: Cargo documentation / air waybill processing → Cargo and Freight Agents documentation task. WORKBank overlay available (information task).
Dangerous goods documentation maps partly to freight-agent hazmat paperwork; the regulatory ACCEPTANCE decision is higher-agency and should be reviewed (consider H4).
Check-in / boarding pass issuance → ticket agent task. WORKBank overlay available.
Special assistance / de-escalation is interpersonal and high-agency; no clean WORKBank agent overlay — pipeline should tag 'model-inferred' and likely H4–H5 / LOW_PRIORITY for agent automation.
Loadsheet / weight-and-balance → cargo load-planning. Safety sign-off keeps human agency high (H4) even where capability is moderate → RED_LIGHT.

PHYSICAL handling task. Intentionally has NO WORKBank overlay — automation here is a robotics/GSE lever, not an AI-agent lever. Pipeline must tag 'model-inferred' and surface it as a different lever, not a software-agent opportunity.
